newsitem.title: USA: Asian exporters cautious for next 12 months - DHL.
newsitem.headline: Asian exporters cautious for next 12 months - DHL.

text.p: Asia-Pacific exporters are more bullish on their five-year outlook than their 12-month prospects, the second quarterly DHL Asia Pacific Export Indicator survey said.
The poll, conducted by the Gallup Organization for DHL Worldwide Express, asked 1,125 senior executives of large Asian exporting companies between June 22 and August 2 to rate their export prospects.
Seventy-five executives in each of 15 countries took part.
At least 50 percent of the respondents in nine of the 15 rated their sales prospects for the next 12 months as good or excellent.
Exporters in Vietnam (84 percent), India (78 percent) and Malaysia (77 percent) were the most optimistic.
Chinese exporters, in contrast, were highly pessimistic; two-thirds of Chinese respondents rated their prospects as fair or poor.

Optimism rose when the survey asks respondents to rate their export prospects over five years. In 11 countries, a majority had good or excellent expectations, and fewer than 20 percent felt their orders would not grow.

Exporters in Vietnam (91 percent) and Australia (84 percent) rated their five-year prospects as good or excellent. Less than half the respondents in Taiwan, China, Thailand and Sri Lanka felt optimistic.

When asked to which of their export markets they expected to export more in the next 12 months, most cited other Asian nations, but 45 percent of exporters in India saw Europe and the Middle East as their best growth market while 49 percent of respondents in the Philippines cited the U.S.
However, a majority of all Asia Pacific exporters identified the U.S. as their leading export target.
Most respondents said they expected that Hong Kong would be better economically, or at least no worse, after the July 1, 1997 transfer of sovereignty to China.

Exporters in Hong Kong, Vietnam, Malaysia and China were most optimistic about the colony's future as part of China. More than one-third of exporters in Australia, Korea, New Zealand and Thailand thought Hong Kong's economy would worsen. -Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
